title: Inspect and extend: Store wallet state without inventing chain truth
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/store.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve key/value adapter, json parsing, corrupt state, and local transaction storage.
problem: Local storage is a notebook, not a blockchain. Read the storage adapter and store tests, then distinguish persisted demo history from provider-synchronized history. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/store.ts` and the related project files: src/store.ts; src/persistence.ts; test/store.test.ts.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to key/value adapter, json parsing, corrupt state, and local transaction storage.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Local changes can survive restarts but are not proof of confirmed on-chain transactions.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: Local storage is a notebook, not a blockchain. Read the storage adapter and store tests, then distinguish persisted demo history from provider-synchronized history.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/store.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
